notes: Copy in 8 rows holding stone lines 1-19; rows read right to left, top to bottom. Several sign values set from context of recurring words: tedḫelowi (rows 2, 5), terikelowi (rows 3, 5), ato mḫe / at mḫe (row 7). In -lowi groups the sign written S or small 5 just before o is taken as l and the one before it as e, whatever its size. Row 1: rightmost sign hatched (w?); after soreyi-like word the sign before r looks like 4 (read i?, Griffith may intend e); te? group has a dotted (restored) sign rendered [.] and a long horizontal stroke through it. Row 1 hatch before final e has one solid stroke (maybe y). Row 3: [.][.][.] in te[...]ikelowi is a hatched stretch of about 3 sign widths; the c-like sign before k read as ligatured i. Row 4 is the least certain: hooked rising strokes read m?, crossed-loop sign read d?, last group '/ /7' read te o?. Row 5: '4S/S' read l o e? i (no w sign visible). Row 6: '+'-like sign read i?, 'ω·' and 'c·' read to. Row 7: '13' with a loop after p i read s? (could be q). Row 8: Σ-with-long-tail sign is p in pisi and k before te (p/k look the same here). Line numbers placed where Griffith's small numbers stand.
